text:
leila_support: FYI high-sev from Customer B: sudden surge of 500/503s hitting hosted endpoints since 11:22 UTC. they report timeouts and gateway errors across chat and completion routes. customer experiencing ~25% failure rate over last 8m. escalating.

jordan_sre: oncall acknowledging. which error payload are they seeing? 502/503 gateway or upstream 500? any stack snippets?

leila_support: API replies look like: 

  {\n    \"status\": 503,\n    \"error\": \"upstream error\",\n    \"detail\": \"worker terminated unexpectedly\"\n  }

leila_support: they attached a small sample: three consecutive requests produced 500, 503, 503.

metrics-bot: cluster-alert: inference-worker pool=prod-us-west2 restart_spike=9/10m on node group ig-ml-gpu-22. GPU memory_pressure > 92% for ~6m. p99 latency jumped from 120ms -> 780ms.

sam_runtime: any recent model pushes or runtime image flips? deploy-bot?

deploy-bot: deployment event: model redwood-mini-14b-8k-quant_v3 started canary at 11:12 UTC (10% traffic in prod-us-west2). runtime image rrt-2.1.4 deployed to canary nodes at 11:05 UTC.

jordan_sre: likely correlation. nina, collect /var/logs/worker.log from crashing pods and look for CUDA OOM, illegal memory access, or c++ exceptions. also check dmesg for oom_killer.

nina_eng: pulled logs from a restarted pod: 

```
I0420 11:20:58.401 loader.cpp:211] loading model redwood-mini-14b-8k-quant_v3
E0420 11:21:05.002 gpu_allocator.cc:67] CUDA malloc failed: out of memory while allocating 1200MB
W0420 11:21:05.003 kv_cache.cpp:412] kv cache resize failed, requested 9830400 bytes
F0420 11:21:05.004 runtime.cc:512] Fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at 0x7f7fffbad000
*** End of stack trace ***
```

nina_eng: node dmesg shows process killed by cgroup OOM, then container restarted. pattern matches restart_spike.

qa_automation: customer sent repro: batch of 12 requests with prompt lengths 3k-7k tokens, max_gen=1024, concurrency=4. they ran it against v3 canary.

sam_runtime: v3 included an optimization that changes kv layout and reduces memory for most cases but has a corner-case bug increasing peak activation when sequence window > 4096. edge-case rarely triggered in unit tests but seen in long prompts at real scale.

jordan_sre: mitigation: yank v3 traffic immediately. sam, set canary weight to 0 in prod-us-west2 and fail open to stable v2.

sam_runtime: running command: 

```
# routing-control
set-canary-weight --model redwood-mini-14b-8k-quant_v3 --region prod-us-west2 --weight 0
```

sam_runtime: canary weight -> 0% (propagation ~45s). routing now flows to redwood-mini-14b-8k-quant_v2.

metrics-bot: confirmation: redwood-mini-14b-8k-quant_v3 traffic in prod-us-west2 = 0%. global error-rate for impacted endpoints trending back down to baseline in 70s.

jordan_sre: good. next steps: capture core or gcore from a crashing container before it exits. nina, if you can catch one in pre-exit loop, create core and upload to artifacts.

nina_eng: caught a core via on-node gcore, extracted with gdb. backtrace shows top frames in attention kernel and kv_cache. snippet: 

```
#0  0x7f8b12c4 in attention::compute_qk (this=0x7f9d5000, args=...) at attention.cu:278
#1  0x7f8b135e in attention_forward (..) at attention.cu:410
#2  0x7f8b1b33 in infer_step (req=...) at runtime.cc:621
#3  0x4012be in main_worker_loop (..) at worker_main.cpp:89
```

nina_eng: further inspection: index calculation at attention.cu:278 can overflow when (seq_len + prefix) * head_dim > INT32_MAX in intermediate multiply with 32-bit. leads to buffer write beyond allocation. this code path was introduced in v3 quant packing.

jordan_sre: that's a clear bug. root cause: integer overflow in offset computation after the new quant packing path. severity: P1 customer impact. remediation options: revert model artifact v3 -> v2 (done) and patch attention code to use 64-bit arithmetic and bounds checks, plus runtime guard to reject requests that would exceed safe activation estimates.

sam_runtime: I will open an emergency PR to revert the v3 build in the model registry and schedule a follow-up fix for the kernel. also adding a runtime heuristic: if estimated kv_allocation > 12GB (configurable) reject with 413 and descriptive message rather than risk crash. patching now.

nina_eng: created bug MB-4802 and attached core dump, gdb bt, repro harness and failing input set. linking: https://internal/bugs/MB-4802

leila_support: informed Customer B: "We've removed the canary model and routed you back to the stable model. We're actively debugging and will provide ETA. For immediate relief, you can cap max_tokens=512 or set model=redwood-mini-14b-8k-quant_v2." customer appreciates quick response.

jordan_sre: ops follow-up: add alert: inference-worker restart_count > 4 in 10m -> PagerDuty. also add an SLO alert if error-rate > 5% for 5m.

metrics-bot: post-mitigation stats: restart_spike resolved; p99 latency down to 140ms; error-rate back to 1.5%.

sam_runtime: rollback in model registry done and promoted stable v2. hotfix PR created: runtime#2345 adding 64-bit offsets + bounds check + preflight estimator. unit tests added for sequences > 8k. CI running.

nina_eng: test reproducer script committed to MB-4802; it reproduces OOB write on v3 with prompt ~6k tokens and batch size 12. include reproducer steps in bug.

jordan_sre: action items summary:
- sam: revert v3 in registry (done) and land runtime guard PR (in progress).
- nina: attach artifacts to bug and coordinate with model-build for new quant packing.
- leila: update customer and offer config mitigations.
- ops: add restart_count and error-rate alerts.

leila_support: Customer B confirmed reduced errors and will monitor. closing loop with them once PR landed and new safe model build available.

deploy-bot: confirm: redwood-mini-14b-8k-quant_v3 traffic = 0% in prod-us-west2, deployment artifacts marked rolled_back.

jordan_sre: thanks everyone. we'll keep thread open until runtime patch and model rebuild validated in canary with safety checks.

qa_automation: noted: added long-prompt integration test to CI against quant builds to catch this earlier.

metrics-bot: final: baseline restored. keeping a 6h watch window for restart regressions.
